title: Steve: "can you resume the portfolio work"
body: Then, mid-session: *"note, you can spawn codex agents via the codex cli."*

title: Why c1-1 failed five times — measured before dispatching a sixth
body:
Every refusal was the key-light gate (0.012, 0.0277, 0.0122, 0.0162, 0.0133 against 0.011). Replicating the gate and attributing its vector: identical with and without the water-cut edges, so the water is not it; net direction 86° (straight down the image); the two darkest luma bands carry all of it; every block of the cell contributes, the pure-forest blocks most. **A dense conifer canopy reads as a sun from above** — each crown a pale top over a dark skirt, and the skirt-to-next-top edge points the same way for every tree. The accepted neighbours read 0.002.

Seam tone (27.3 vs the sound coast) was located to seven eighths of the north edge, where the candidate painted forest over the coast's arriving ground. And the briefs were stale against c0-1's rebake: the stated water crossing was 32%, the art has it at 22%.

The brief was rewritten to say exactly those three things, and c1-1 dispatched alone.

title: Sixth refusal — stopped. This is the owner's ruling, not another brief
body: Key-light 0.016, worse, same signature. The worker's own report: *"conifer crowns and basalt retain visibly brighter upper detail and darker lower detail; the literal one-flat-value rule is not met."* It also painted forest over the coast's arriving pixels a second time. Two strikes on the mechanism with the fix in place, so no seventh candidate. Four options are written up in STATE.md for the morning: a canopy-aware measure, a dark-forest limit, acceptance on the eye, or compositing the neighbours' pixels back over the outer band before the gates run.

title: The brief writer read the wrong thing
body: It read each neighbour's water mask at the exact edge column; the continuity gate reads the land layer's alpha within 8 px of the line. c5-2's beck reaches the line a few pixels short of the column, so the gate demanded a crossing the brief never named, and c6-2 was refused for not meeting it. The writer now reads what the gate reads. Six briefs were then rewritten to name the exact defect and number each cell was last refused for, and dispatched as one run.

title: Steve: "can you change the codex agent you use to astra 6"
body: Applied as lock change 18: the dispatch model in cell.mjs is now `gpt-6-astra`. The first three astra dispatches then died in 0.1 min — *"requires a newer version of Codex"* — because the CLI on PATH was 0.149 while the app carried 0.153. The pipeline now runs the newest Codex on the machine; Steve also updated the CLI. Astra confirmed working: *ASTRA OK*.

title: Steve: have Codex review the image gen before Claude does, to cut the cycles — and use it as a pair
body:
*"I was thinking more of having codex review the image gen before your review to try and reduce how many cycles we are doing ya know? Also as a human dev we value the rubber ducky approach... astra is new so im curious how it works out."* Then: *"works for me."*

So: a review-and-retry loop goes into the runner (Codex reviews every refused candidate against the brief and the gate block, the worker gets one more attempt with those notes, then it comes to Claude), and this page exists so the exchanges can be read.

title: c3-1 is the first trial of the review loop
body: Refused on one gate only (a stream sent out the south edge it was told to keep dry). Claude's read is written and sealed first; the same evidence goes to Codex blind; the two are compared before the second attempt is dispatched with the reviewer's addendum.

title: After the review: Codex was right about the south seam, and I had rationalised the gate
body:
Codex saw blue water continuing across the south seam into c3-2 at the refused position and said the gate’s “nearest none” conflicted with the neighbour’s paint. Checked: c3-2’s cut water DOES reach the seam at 62% — alpha 0 on the first row inside the cell — but only about 20 px wide there, under the gate’s 30 px minimum run, so the gate sees no crossing and refuses any continuation of a stream that visibly exists. My sealed read had accepted the gate’s word for it. The worker did the sensible thing and continued the visible stream.

So the second attempt cannot simply say “no water south”: the edit target hands the worker c3-2’s stream in its bottom 12 m. The clean fix is to widen c3-2’s water cut at the seam (a mask edit and re-derive, no regeneration — the method Steve asked for on c0-1) so the brief writer states the arrival and c3-1 can carry it on. c3-2 is accepted art, so that is Steve’s call. Codex also found the pool undersized (9.7 m against 15), the north inlet not connected to it, the groove drawn as a kerb, the panels crown-sized, and a brief contradiction (“2-3 m wide the whole way” against a measured 5 m arrival). All right.

images.caption: c3-2 at its north seam near 62%: the painted stream (top) reaches the seam; its water cut (bottom, white) reaches it too, but ~20 px wide

title: The measurement Codex asked for, run: the threshold makes the number
body:
Signed vertical-gradient sums split at the gate’s 12-unit floor, alpha-safe, all on the retained mass:

```
cell                         retained gy   dropped gy   together
c1-1 candidate 6 (refused)      +16.04       -17.44      -1.40
ninjaone c2-0 forest (accepted)  +6.79        -7.43      -0.64
ninjaone c3-2 forest (accepted)  -0.33        -0.60      -0.93
c1-2 candidate (forest+coast)    +4.29        -1.96      +2.33
c0-1 meadow (accepted)           +0.59        -1.04      -0.46
```

In c1-1 the darkest band alone carries +11.2 retained against -10.8 dropped. The gate keeps the sharp half of every crown (dark skirt against brighter ground below) and drops the soft half (bright top fading into the skirt), and reads the difference as a sun from above. Codex’s caveat stands too: any image’s unthresholded sum telescopes to its edges, so cancellation alone does not prove the shading is permitted — the worker still admits shaded crowns. What the measurement settles is that 0.011 cannot separate a shaded canopy from a sun, and that the accepted NinjaOne forest carries the same signature. Codex’s proposal goes to Steve with the rest: before another full cell, generate one small flat-light forest study, let him rule on its look, and calibrate what a compliant dense canopy measures.

title: Steve: widen c3-2’s cut at the seam — “Sure thing” — and choose models per role
body:
*"Sure thing, also you are free to spawn codex threads of varying efforts so if 5.6 was the better image gen go for it and let astra be the rubber ducky or w.e. you feel is unblocking you best."*

So: c3-2’s water cut gets widened at the seam (mask only, re-derived, no regeneration) once the run releases the lock; the generation model and effort become switchable per dispatch instead of hardcoded; astra reviews. c4-2’s 9.8 MB edit target went through astra’s image tool, so c4-0’s rejection was a one-off and astra stays on generation for now.

title: c6-2 on astra: ten of eleven gates, missing only the west beck
body: The north edge — 65 m of bay arriving from c6-1 — was met this time; the first candidate had carried the quarry floor 40 m too far east. What remains unmet is c5-2’s beck a quarter of the way down the west edge, the crossing the brief writer only learned to name tonight. The worker’s own report flags disconnected drainage and directional shading. This is exactly the case for the review loop: one reviewer pass, one retry with its notes.
